classification_reasons: Spec tightness: tight - both of spec.md's flagged concerns (empty-input raises ValueError, parameter type is Collection[float]) are closed with a recorded decision in evidence/decisions-b.json (item 1: the ValueError guard-clause behaviour; item 2: Collection[float], explicitly marked overturned from the panel's Sequence[float] pick), and Acceptance is fully measurable (mean([1,2,3,4])==2.5, mean([5])==5.0, mean([]) raises ValueError, mean({1.0,2.0,3.0})==2.0, 9 passed, ruff clean, silent compileall).

Blast radius: small - the source diff touches exactly the files plan.md lists (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py) plus the change folder and status.yaml bookkeeping; no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and no sdlc.yaml risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config, confirmed by reading sdlc.yaml directly) appear in the diff; no schema, contract or migration change; mean has no existing caller so add/divide/percent are unaffected.

Test coverage: mean is brand-new code with no pre-existing test covering it before this change - the build supplies its own four tests - so the third routine criterion (code the existing tests already cover) fails and the plan stays non-routine.
attempted: Intent: read intent.md fresh. The diff (unchanged since the prior 'continue' verdict at b23dc6d) adds mean(values) returning the arithmetic mean as a float, resolves the two open questions intent.md left (empty input -> ValueError, parameter type -> Collection[float]), exports it from __init__.py/__all__, and covers normal, single-element, empty and non-Sequence-Collection cases in tests/test_calc.py. This is exactly intent's Proposed outcome, nothing extra, nothing missing. The one intent item not in this diff - a proposed one-line CLAUDE.md Layout update - is explicitly scoped by intent/plan to the build PR description, not the repo, so its absence is expected.

Spec and plan: read spec.md and plan.md directly and compared against the current sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py and tests/test_calc.py on disk (not just the diff hunks). calc.py's mean body (guard clause raising ValueError, then divide(sum(values), len(values)), collections.abc.Collection import) matches plan.md step 1 verbatim, including the reconciled note that ruff's format-on-edit hook rewrote typing.Collection to collections.abc.Collection; __init__.py's import line and __all__ match step 2 exactly (alphabetical, between divide and percent); the four tests in tests/test_calc.py match step 3's names and assertions exactly. No file changed outside plan.md's Files-that-change list. This round's own diff (since the last reviewed commit) is confined to status.yaml (iteration bump 1->2, panel_calls 0->1, timestamps) and evidence/run-c.json (run timer restart) - no source, spec or plan content changed in this round, consistent with the delegation prompt's description, which I verified rather than took on faith.

Proof: compared evidence/verifier.md against the diff's four new tests; it names all four individually (via 'pytest -k mean -v'), reports 9 passed matching the diff's added test count, and exercises exactly the pinned behaviours (empty raises ValueError not ZeroDivisionError, a set works, add/divide/percent unaffected, a generator is still rejected via TypeError at len()). No test.log/build.log/lint.log are committed at this phase; I independently confirmed (by reading framework/plugin/gate/artifacts.py's REQUIRED_EVIDENCE mapping, not by quoting the panel's or reviewer's claim) that REQUIRED_EVIDENCE['c'] = (verifier.md,) only, and that the three logs are required starting at phase (d) - so their absence at (c) is correct per the framework's own deterministic mapping, not a gap.

Blast radius: mean is additive and uncalled elsewhere; divide is called, not modified; __all__ gains one name in the correct alphabetical slot. No guardrail file, no sdlc.yaml risk_list item (verified directly against sdlc.yaml's risk_list: auth, data migrations, money movement, production config), no schema or config file appears in the diff. status.yaml is not a guardrail file under this project's definition and its diff is only the phase/timestamp/iteration/panel_calls bump expected at this point in the workflow.

Policies: coding-standards' export-pattern and type-hint rules are met (Collection[float] hint, alphabetical import/__all__ placement matching add/divide/percent, no docstring inconsistency beyond the one plan.md itself flags and justifies); no new dependency, statistics.mean is not wrapped; security-baseline, ux-conventions and data-conventions are correctly inapplicable to a pure in-process arithmetic helper with no I/O, UI or stored data.

Tests: test_mean, test_mean_single_element, test_mean_empty and test_mean_accepts_non_sequence_collection each pin a distinct behaviour (correct averaging, single-element division, the explicit ValueError guard rather than a fallthrough ZeroDivisionError from divide, and the widened Collection[float]-not-Sequence contract via a set); manually traced each assertion against the guard-clause-plus-divide implementation on disk and found no case where a plausible bug (wrong exception type, Sequence-only implementation, off-by-one in the guard) would still pass. No pre-existing test (test_add, test_divide_by_zero_raises, test_percent, test_percent_zero_whole_raises, tests/test_flag.py) is touched or weakened; this is a feature-type change (status.yaml: change_type: feature), so the fix-type 'do not touch existing tests' rule does not even apply, and it is honored anyway.

Process/park history: independently read framework/plugin/gate/checks.py's check_panel to verify the delegation prompt's claim that the prior park was a tooling false positive rather than trusting the claim. Confirmed check_panel now calls ledger.load_ledgers (plural, across phases up to the current one) and matches spec.md's 'decided (by panel): ...' closing text as a prefix of decisions-b.json item 1's decision text ('mean() requires at least one value...raised explicitly by mean itself via a guard clause (not inherited from divide)'), which is a genuine, pre-existing panel decision from phase (b), not a fabricated one. This is a process/tooling fix outside the diff under review (the fix lives in installed framework code, not in changes/0002's files) and I judge only the diff, per instructions; I did not treat the earlier park, the earlier escalate-then-continue panel round, or the stale prior verdict's commit mismatch as reasons against this diff, since none of those are properties of the diff itself.
